documents.title: Generative AI Guidance
documents.summary: UWM-wide guidance on responsible GenAI use. It sets general principles (follow law, verify output, protect data by risk level) and sets no stance on student use in courses.
documents.stance_why: The page says users "should" follow guidelines on law, accuracy, security and data privacy but never says whether students may use AI for coursework; it points to the Center for Advancing Student Learning, so it sets no stance and delegates.

units.why: The intro says UWM "is committed to providing students with the knowledge, skills and experience necessary to sustain success in an AI-driven world", a career-readiness rationale for engaging with AI, so P44 (informs).
units.anchor: committed to providing students with the knowledge, skills and experience necessary
units.frag_start: The University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee is committed

units.why: "the following guidelines should be adhered to when utilizing Generative AI tools" sets the purpose and scope of an institution-wide set of principles, so P56 (framework) rather than a specific rule type.
units.anchor: the following guidelines should be adhered to when utilizing Generative AI tools
units.frag_start: As part of the university’s commitment

units.why: "Do not use the tools in an unethical way or as part of any illegal activity" and comply with acceptable use policies: a duty to follow law and existing university policy, so P77.
units.anchor: Do not use the tools in an unethical way or as part of any illegal
units.frag_start: Do not use the tools

units.why: Administrators of GenAI tools "should keep up to date on relevant changes to laws, regulations and policies", a duty to stay informed, so P102.
units.anchor: you should keep up to date on relevant changes to laws, regulations and policies
units.frag_start: If you are administering Generative AI tools

units.why: Users "should consult with the Information Security Office or the Center for Advancing Student Learning" with acceptable-use questions; it directs readers to offices for guidance, so P115.
units.anchor: should consult with the Information Security Office or the Center for Advancing Student Learning
units.frag_start: Individuals who use Generative AI platforms

units.why: "One should always review the output ... to verify that the information provided is correct", because GenAI can hallucinate; this is verify-output, P31.
units.anchor: One should always review the output from Generative AI tools for potential bias
units.frag_start: One should always review
units.frag_end: citations or quotations included in the output are legitimate

units.why: The sentence "if you are building an AI system, be transparent about the AI components" with documentation of model and training data is about documenting deployed AI systems, P98.
units.anchor: if you are building an AI system, be transparent about the AI components
units.frag_start: Additionally, if you are building
units.frag_end: increasing trust in a Generative AI Tool

units.why: "consult with the Information Security Office about security measures" to protect model, training data and content from unauthorized access is a security-controls rule, P126.
units.anchor: consult with the Information Security Office about security measures
units.frag_start: Whether you are looking to utilize AI tools

units.why: "Research tools to better understand potential biases" asks users to assess tools before use; P117 (evaluate a tool) is closest, P53 does not fit since no harm is stated as a rule.
units.anchor: Research tools to better understand potential biases that may be present in their model
units.frag_start: Research tools to better understand

units.why: "Learn more about prompt engineering so you can better understand how your prompts affect potential outputs" is practical advice on prompting, P93.
units.anchor: Learn more about prompt engineering
units.frag_start: Learn more about prompt engineering

units.why: "UWM is legally and ethically obligated to protect individual and institutional data" and tools train on prompts so input "could be accessed by anyone"; a privacy statement, P50.
units.anchor: will use the prompts that users input as part of the training data
units.frag_start: Many Generative AI tools

units.why: Low-risk data use cases "are approved by UWM IT" for local, private-cloud and public-cloud use; a data-classification-based approval, P65 (approval of tool use), not a ban.
units.anchor: Use cases involving low risk data are approved by UWM IT
units.frag_start: Use cases involving low risk data
units.fit_note: Approves low-risk data uses rather than reviewing a tool.

units.why: For medium risk data, users must "contact the information security office ... to review your use case" and discuss de-identification; a review requirement, P65.
units.anchor: contact the information security office
units.frag_start: For use cases involving medium risk data

units.why: For high risk data such as PHI or PII, "contact the information security office ... to review your use case"; same review mechanism for a higher tier, P65.
units.anchor: For use cases involving high risk data, including protected health information
units.frag_start: For use cases involving high risk data

units.why: Human-subject research data requires contacting "the Institutional Review Board" plus security and research computing; research-data rule, P62.
units.anchor: For use cases involving human-subject research data, contact the Institutional Review Board
units.frag_start: For use cases involving human-subject research data

documents.title: Syllabus Statements: Guiding Student Generative AI Usage in Your Class
tiers: Allowing the full use of Generative AI
documents.summary: CASL page with a course checklist and three sample syllabus statements (full use, specific use, prohibition) plus citation and misconduct language. Instructors choose which to adopt.
documents.stance_why: It offers three sample statements ("Allowing the Full Use", "Allowing Specific AI Use", "Prohibiting AI Use") and tells each instructor to "Explicitly state your expectations", so the page itself takes no single stance and delegates.

units.why: "Explicitly state your expectations for student Generative AI use in the syllabus" is a checklist duty for each course, P09.
units.anchor: Explicitly state your expectations for student Generative AI use in the syllabus.
units.frag_start: Explicitly state your expectations

units.why: Instructors "talk directly with students about your Generative AI policy, sharing examples of what is and is not appropriate use", going beyond listing the rule, so P66.
units.anchor: talk directly with students about your Generative AI policy
units.frag_start: Include written expectations for Generative AI use

units.why: "provide information on how students are expected to cite Generative AI use" tells instructors to supply citation instructions; closest is P24 though the rule is the instructor duty to explain citation.
units.anchor: provide information on how students are expected to cite Generative AI use for assignments
units.frag_start: If applicable, provide information
units.fit_note: Addressed to instructors: supply citation expectations, not the student duty itself.

units.why: The first sample says "you may use Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) for assignments with appropriate citations", a permit-by-default with citation, P02.
units.anchor: you may use Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) for assignments with appropriate citations
units.frag_start: In this class, you may use

units.frag_start: AI-generated messages and media may be biased

units.why: "you must cite Generative AI when it is used" is a disclosure duty with each submission, P24.
